examples.en: Busan is a metropolitan city, so there are many people.

examples.ko: 광역 버스를 타면 서울까지 빨리 갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you take the wide-area bus, you can reach Seoul quickly.
If a regional railway opens, commuting gets easier.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 광역 상수도로 물을 받아요.
examples.en: This area gets water from the regional water supply.
Metropolitan cities have many universities and big hospitals.

examples.ko: 광역 단체장 선거가 다음 주에 있어요.
examples.en: The election for the head of the regional government is next week.

explain: '광역'은 한 도시만이 아니라 여러 도시가 이어진 넓은 지역을 말해요. 한국에서는 '광역시'와 '광역버스'가 가장 많이 쓰여요. 서울은 '특별시', 부산·대구·인천 같은 큰 도시는 '광역시'라고 불러요.
explain_en: 광역 means a wide region that joins several cities, not just one. In Korea you meet it most in 광역시 and 광역버스. Seoul is a 특별시, while big cities such as Busan, Daegu and Incheon are called 광역시.

en: coastal waters; adjoining seas; near seas

examples.en: This boat only fishes in coastal waters.

examples.ko: 요즘 근해에서 잡히는 오징어가 많이 줄었어요.
examples.en: The amount of squid caught in the near seas has dropped a lot lately.
The waves are high even in the coastal waters today, so be careful.

examples.ko: 태풍 때문에 근해를 지나던 배들이 모두 항구로 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: Because of the typhoon, all the ships passing through the coastal waters came back to port.

examples.ko: 아버지는 젊을 때 근해로 나가는 고기잡이배를 탔어요.
examples.en: When my father was young, he worked on a fishing boat that went out to the near seas.

examples.ko: 근해 날씨가 나빠서 오늘은 배가 안 떠요.
examples.en: The weather in the coastal waters is bad, so no boats are leaving today.

explain: 육지에서 가까운 바다를 말해요. 반대로 먼 바다는 '원양'이라고 하고, 뉴스에서는 '근해 어업'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to the sea close to land. The opposite, the distant ocean, is '원양', and on the news you often hear it in phrases like '근해 어업' (coastal fishing).

examples.en: Every weekend I walk along the path on the riverbank.
Cherry blossoms are in full bloom on both sides of the embankment path.
It rained, so the embankment path is very slippery.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 이 둑길로 학교에 다녔어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I went to school along this embankment path.

examples.ko: 저녁에 둑길에서 자전거를 타는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: In the evening, many people ride bikes on the embankment path.

examples.ko: 둑길이 끝나는 곳에 작은 다리가 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small bridge where the embankment path ends.

explain: '둑'은 물을 막으려고 쌓은 언덕이고, '둑길'은 그 위나 옆으로 난 길이에요. 강이나 저수지 옆 산책길, 시골 풍경을 이야기할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '둑' is a bank built to hold back water, and '둑길' is the path on top of it or beside it. It often comes up when talking about walking paths by rivers or reservoirs and about the countryside.

examples.en: My father works at a neighborhood carpenter's shop.
I left a chair to be repaired at the carpenter's shop.

examples.ko: 목공소 사장님이 나무로 책장을 짜 주셨어요.
examples.en: The owner of the carpentry shop built a bookshelf out of wood for me.

examples.ko: 우리 집 앞에는 오래된 목공소가 있어요.
examples.en: There is an old carpentry shop in front of my house.

examples.ko: 톱밥 냄새가 나서 목공소 안을 들여다봤어요.
examples.en: I smelled sawdust and peeked inside the carpentry shop.
The carpentry shop is closed today.

explain: 나무로 가구나 물건을 만들고 고치는 곳이에요. 일하는 사람은 '목수'라고 하고, 취미로 배우는 곳은 '목공방'이라고도 부르는 경우가 있어요.
explain_en: It is a place that makes and repairs wooden furniture and goods. The worker is a '목수', and places where people learn woodworking as a hobby are sometimes called '목공방'.

examples.en: At the national cemetery, the graves spread out over a wide area.
I visited the cemetery with my family during the holiday.
I bought flowers at the entrance of the cemetery.
We tidied up the area around the cemetery.
Independence activists are enshrined in this cemetery.
The road to the cemetery is steep.

explain: '무덤'이 하나하나의 무덤이라면, 묘역은 무덤이 모여 있는 구역 전체를 말해요. 가족 무덤이 있는 곳은 '산소'라고도 하고, 국립묘지나 공원처럼 넓은 곳은 묘역이라고 많이 불러요. 말투가 조금 공식적이에요.
explain_en: While '무덤' is a single grave, 묘역 is the whole area where graves are gathered. A family grave site is also called '산소', and large places such as national cemeteries or memorial parks are often called 묘역. The tone is a bit formal.

examples.en: The ship finally reached land.
Island people go out to the mainland to shop.

examples.ko: 오랜만에 뭍을 밟으니 땅이 흔들리는 것 같아요.
examples.en: Stepping on land after so long, it feels like the ground is swaying.

examples.ko: 물고기는 뭍에서 오래 살 수 없어요.
examples.en: Fish can't live long on land.

examples.ko: 뭍과 섬을 잇는 다리가 새로 생겼어요.
examples.en: A new bridge connecting the mainland and the island has been built.

examples.ko: 뭍이 멀어서 아플 때 병원에 가기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The mainland is far, so it's hard to get to a hospital when you're sick.

explain: 바다나 섬과 대비해서 땅, 육지를 가리킬 때 써요. '육지'로 바꿔 말해도 되지만 '뭍'은 순우리말이라 이야기나 글에서 더 부드러운 느낌이에요. 받침 때문에 '뭍이[무치]', '뭍에[무테]'처럼 소리 나요.
explain_en: It points to land or dry ground in contrast with the sea or an island. You can replace it with '육지', but '뭍' is a native Korean word and feels softer in stories and writing. Because of the final consonant it sounds like '뭍이[무치]' and '뭍에[무테]'.

examples.en: Greece is the birthplace of the Olympics.

examples.ko: 이 학교 자리가 근대 교육의 발상지래요.
examples.en: I heard this school site is the cradle of modern education.
That place is famous as the birthplace of jazz.

examples.ko: 이곳이 그 운동의 발상지라는 표지판이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a sign saying this is where the movement began.
I went to see the monument built at the birthplace.

examples.ko: 문화의 발상지를 따라 걷는 여행 코스가 인기예요.
examples.en: A trip route that follows the cradles of culture is popular.

explain: 문화, 운동, 사상, 제도가 처음 시작된 곳을 말해요. 강이 시작되는 곳은 '발원지'라고 하니까 구별해서 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the place where a culture, movement, idea or system first began. The place where a river begins is called '발원지', so keep the two apart.

examples.ko: 할머니는 매주 일요일마다 법당에 가서 기도해요.
examples.en: My grandmother goes to the temple hall every Sunday to pray.
You have to be quiet inside the main hall.

examples.ko: 절에 가면 먼저 법당 앞에서 인사를 해요.
examples.en: When I go to a temple, I first bow in front of the main hall.
You take off your shoes when you enter the main hall.

examples.ko: 큰 법당 안에 부처님 상이 모셔져 있어요.
examples.en: A Buddha statue is enshrined in the big main hall.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 법당 처마 밑에서 잠깐 쉬었어요.
examples.en: It rained, so I rested for a while under the eaves of the main hall.

explain: 법당은 절 안에서 부처님을 모신 건물이에요. 절 전체는 '절'이나 '사찰'이라고 해요. 종교마다 예배하는 건물을 부르는 말이 달라서 교회, 성당처럼 따로 써요.
explain_en: A 법당 is the building inside a temple where the Buddha is enshrined. The whole temple compound is called '절' or '사찰'. Each religion has its own word for its place of worship, such as 교회 or 성당.

examples.en: This company moved its base to Busan.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 본거지인 서울을 떠나 제주에서 살아요.
examples.en: That singer left Seoul, his home base, and lives on Jeju.
A football team's base is the city where its stadium is.
This place is our club's home base.
This area has been a base for merchants since long ago.
Where would be a good place for our new base?

explain: '본사'는 회사에만 쓰지만 '본거지'는 팀, 모임, 단체, 사람처럼 활동의 중심이 되는 곳에 폭넓게 써요. 뉴스에서는 어떤 단체의 활동 중심지를 가리킬 때 나오고, 일상에서는 '아지트'나 '근거지'처럼 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: '본사' is only for companies, but '본거지' is used widely for the center of activity of a team, club, group or person. In the news it names the main place where a group operates, and in daily talk people may also say '아지트' or '근거지'.

en: birthplace house; childhood home of a famous person

examples.en: We visited the poet's birthplace.
The birthplace house was turned into a museum.

examples.ko: 그분의 생가는 작은 시골 마을에 있어요.
examples.en: His birthplace is in a small country village.
On the weekend I took photos in front of the birthplace.
The restoration work on the birthplace is finished.
I'm touring the birthplace of a famous painter.

explain: 유명한 사람이 태어난 집에 쓰는 말이라서 보통 사람에게는 잘 안 써요. 평범한 사람이 태어나 자란 집은 '고향집'이라고 해요. 박물관이나 관광지 안내에서 '생가'를 자주 봐요.
explain_en: It is used for the house where a famous person was born, so it is rarely used for ordinary people. The house an ordinary person grew up in is called '고향집'. You often see '생가' on museum and tourist signs.

examples.en: When the family gathers, the house gets lively and noisy.

examples.ko: 시끌벅적한 시장 골목을 걷다 보면 활기가 느껴져요.
examples.en: Walking through the bustling market alley, you can feel the energy.
The kids run around chattering noisily.

examples.ko: 옆집이 시끌벅적해서 어젯밤에 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The next-door house was so noisy that I couldn't sleep last night.

examples.ko: 시끌벅적 떠들던 교실이 선생님이 들어오자 조용해졌어요.
examples.en: The classroom, which had been buzzing with noise, went quiet when the teacher came in.

examples.ko: 축제 때문에 거리가 하루 종일 시끌벅적했어요.
examples.en: The street was noisy and lively all day because of the festival.

explain: '시끄럽다'는 소음이 불편하다는 느낌이 강하지만 '시끌벅적'은 사람이 많아서 떠들썩하고 활기찬 느낌일 때도 많아요. 보통 '시끌벅적하다'로 쓰고, 부사처럼 '시끌벅적 떠들다'라고도 해요. 반대말은 '조용하다'예요.
explain_en: '시끄럽다' stresses that noise is bothersome, but '시끌벅적' often feels lively, with many people chatting. It is usually used as '시끌벅적하다', and also adverbially as in '시끌벅적 떠들다'. The opposite is '조용하다'.

examples.en: After the KTX was built, the whole country became reachable within a day.

examples.ko: 서울에서 부산까지 일일생활권이라 당일치기 출장도 가능해요.
examples.en: Seoul to Busan is within a day's reach, so a same-day business trip is possible.

examples.ko: 일일생활권 덕분에 지방 사람들도 서울 병원을 쉽게 다녀요.
examples.en: Thanks to day-trip distances, people from the provinces visit Seoul hospitals easily.

examples.ko: 교통이 좋아지면 일일생활권은 더 넓어질 거예요.
examples.en: As transportation improves, the one-day zone will get even wider.
Our country is small, so everywhere is grouped within a one-day zone.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 아직 일일생활권에 들어오지 못했어요.
examples.en: This region hasn't yet come within the one-day zone.

explain: 하루 안에 다녀올 수 있는 거리나 범위를 말해요. 교통 뉴스에서 '일일생활권이 되다/에 들다'처럼 많이 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '당일치기로 다녀올 수 있다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to a distance or area you can travel to and come back from within one day. In transport news it appears as '일일생활권이 되다/에 들다', and in everyday talk people say '당일치기로 다녀올 수 있다'.

en: drive; travel along a road (of a vehicle, formal)

examples.ko: 이 차는 한 번 충전하면 500킬로미터를 주행해요.
examples.en: This car can run 500 km on a single charge.
It is safer to drive slowly on snowy roads.
While driving on the highway, I suddenly got sleepy.

examples.ko: 주행하는 동안 휴대폰을 보면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not look at your phone while driving.

examples.ko: 전기차로 서울에서 부산까지 주행할 수 있을까요?
examples.en: Can an electric car make it from Seoul to Busan?

examples.ko: 시험 삼아 주행해 보니 승차감이 아주 좋았어요.
examples.en: When I took it for a test drive, the ride was very comfortable.

explain: '운전하다'는 사람이 차를 모는 일이고, '주행하다'는 차가 달리는 상태에 초점이 있어요. 그래서 자동차 설명서나 광고, 뉴스에서 '주행 거리', '주행 중'처럼 많이 보여요. 친구에게는 보통 '운전해요'라고 말해요.
explain_en: 운전하다 is a person driving a car, while 주행하다 focuses on the car running. It shows up in manuals, ads and news as 주행 거리 (distance driven) or 주행 중 (while driving). Talking to a friend, you would normally say 운전해요.

examples.en: Barbed wire is put up around the military base.
My clothes tore as I climbed over the barbed wire.
They put barbed wire around the construction site.
A cat passed by beyond the barbed wire.
They made a fence out of barbed wire to protect the field.

examples.ko: 가시가 날카로워서 이 철조망은 만지면 위험해요.
examples.en: The barbs are sharp, so it is dangerous to touch this fence.

explain: '철조망을 치다', '철조망을 넘다'처럼 같이 쓰는 동사를 함께 기억하세요. 일반 울타리는 '울타리'나 '담'이라고 하고, 철조망은 군부대나 경계선처럼 막으려는 목적이 강한 곳에 써요. 뉴스에서는 남북 경계의 철조망 이야기가 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Learn the verbs that go with it: 철조망을 치다 (put up) and 철조망을 넘다 (climb over). An ordinary fence is 울타리 or 담, while 철조망 is used where keeping people out is the point, like military bases and borders. News stories often mention the barbed wire along the border between the two Koreas.

examples.en: Lots of fish are caught in this stretch of sea.
A warning was issued for the waters as the typhoon approached.
The ships went around the dangerous waters.
A drill is being held in the waters near our country.
The water temperature differs from one sea area to another.
The rescue team arrived at the accident site at sea.

explain: 해역은 뉴스나 일기예보에서 '인근 해역', '사고 해역'처럼 바다의 한 구역을 가리킬 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '바다'라고 해요. 강이나 호수 같은 곳은 '수역'이라고 해요.
explain_en: In the news and weather forecasts, this points to one area of the sea, as in '인근 해역' (nearby waters) and '사고 해역' (accident site at sea). In daily conversation people just say '바다' (sea). For rivers and lakes, the word is '수역'.

examples.en: Chuncheon, the city by the lake, has beautiful scenery.
There is a walking path along the lakeshore.
I rode a bike by the lake on the weekend.

examples.ko: 호반 카페에서 커피를 마시며 석양을 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the sunset while drinking coffee at a lakeside cafe.

examples.ko: 이 호텔은 호반에 있어서 전망이 좋아요.
examples.en: This hotel is on the lakeshore, so the view is nice.
The road leading to the lakeside is colored with autumn leaves.

explain: '호숫가'와 같은 뜻이지만 글이나 관광 안내, 카페·호텔 이름에서 더 자주 보여요. 호수 자체가 아니라 그 가장자리를 말해요. '호반의 도시'처럼 호수가 있는 도시를 소개할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It means the same as '호숫가' but is seen more in writing, tourist guides and the names of cafes and hotels. It refers to the edge of the lake, not the lake itself. It is also used to introduce a city by a lake, as in '호반의 도시'.
